safety_verdicts.content: Patient presents with lip swelling for the past 1 hour.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts note lip swelling but do not state the duration as “past 1 hour” (no equivalent time-from-onset duration given).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the time-from-onset (about ~1 hour since exposure/onset) reduces clinical clarity for assessing trajectory and documenting evolution of a potentially life-threatening allergic reaction. In this case, emergent escalation still occurred, so the main impact is loss of temporal detail for handoff/records.

safety_verdicts.content: The patient initially experienced a weird sensation around the lips.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold notes an initial ‘weird sensation around the lips’; generated facts describe swelling onset location (left corner) and pulsating sensation but do not capture the initial ‘weird sensation’ symptom.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not capturing the initial “weird sensation” around the lips removes a minor early symptom detail but does not materially change recognition or management of the apparent allergic reaction already dominated by swelling and breathing symptoms. This is largely documentation granularity rather than a management-changing omission.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold includes dizziness; generated facts do not mention dizziness/lightheadedness.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Dizziness can be a marker of systemic involvement (e.g., hypotension) in anaphylaxis, so omission could reduce perceived severity in downstream documentation or handoff. However, the encounter already triggered emergency response, limiting the likelihood of major clinical impact.

safety_verdicts.content: During consultation, the patient appeared to have breathing difficulties.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states an observed appearance of breathing difficulty during the consultation; generated facts only report patient-reported symptoms and do not include an observed physical finding.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document observed breathing difficulty could understate acuity for emergency services/handoffs, potentially affecting triage urgency in a suspected anaphylactic reaction. Because respiratory compromise is a key red-flag finding, this omission carries meaningful risk even if action was already taken.

Missing this comorbidity may lead to underestimation of risk in subsequent care.
